title: Francis of Assisi Meets the Sultan
text:
In 1219, during the Fifth Crusade, a crusader army was besieging the Egyptian port of Damietta, held by the Ayyubid sultan al-Malik al-Kamil, nephew of Saladin. Francis of Assisi, founder of the Franciscan friars, arrived in the crusader camp. He was dismayed by the soldiers' conduct and warned them against attacking.

Then, with a single companion, he crossed the lines unarmed and walked toward the Muslim camp. He was seized by guards, beaten according to some accounts, and brought before the sultan. Francis had come to preach Christianity to him.

The French bishop Jacques de Vitry, who was in the crusader camp, wrote that the sultan listened attentively to Francis for several days. Al-Kamil did not convert, but he treated Francis with courtesy, and according to Jacques de Vitry he asked Francis to pray for him that God would show him the faith most pleasing to Him. Then the sultan sent him back safely to the Christian camp.

Damietta fell to the crusaders that November, but the crusade ended in failure two years later. Al-Kamil later negotiated the peaceful return of Jerusalem to the Christians with Emperor Frederick II in 1229.
lesson: Even in the middle of a bitter conflict, two people can meet with courtesy and actually listen. Going in person to the other side takes courage, and it is rarely wasted.
people: Francis of Assisi, Sultan al-Malik al-Kamil, Jacques de Vitry
source: Jacques de Vitry, letter of 1220 and Historia Occidentalis; Thomas of Celano, First Life of St. Francis
caveat: Later Franciscan accounts added embellishments, such as an offer to walk through fire, that are not in the earliest sources.
